classification.difficultyReason: Combine triangle angle sums, supplementary angles and the exterior angle theorem across adjacent triangles.

content.prompt: $\angle PRQ=48^{\circ}$ and $\angle TSP=141^{\circ}$. Determine the sizes of every angle.

spec.description: Wide unshaded diagram with P above Q; Q, R, S and T appear in that order along a horizontal straight line. PQ, PR and PS are drawn, with a right-angle square at Q.
spec.mathematics: Q, R, S and T are collinear; PQ is perpendicular to QT. PR divides triangle PQS into adjacent triangles PQR and PRS. Diagram proportions follow the source rather than measured angle sizes.
spec.answerVisibility: Vertex labels and the supplied right-angle mark remain visible. No calculated angles appear in the question diagram.

answer.worked:
Angle sum of triangle $PQR$:
$$\begin{align*}\angle QPR&=180^{\circ}-90^{\circ}-48^{\circ}\\\angle QPR&=42^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
Angles on the straight line $QRS$:
$$\begin{align*}\angle PRS&=180^{\circ}-48^{\circ}\\\angle PRS&=132^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
Angles on the straight line $RST$:
$$\begin{align*}\angle RSP&=180^{\circ}-141^{\circ}\\\angle RSP&=39^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
Exterior angle theorem in triangle $PRS$:
$$\begin{align*}\angle RPS&=141^{\circ}-132^{\circ}\\\angle RPS&=9^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
